name: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
definition: Exercise-related pain along the posteromedial tibial border associated with repetitive loading and bone/periosteal stress.

typical: Diffuse medial tibial pain with running

redFlags.item: Focal severe bony tenderness suggesting stress fracture

investigations.MRI: MRI if focal pain, persistent symptoms or stress fracture is suspected.

amber: Persistent focal pain requires reassessment for stress fracture.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Jangha/Asthi-Snayu overuse phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Exercise-related pain along the posteromedial tibial border associated with repetitive loading and bone/periosteal stress.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, locked joint or other listed red flags.
